questions.micro_topic_tag: Circular vs Linear Convolution Aliasing Boundary
questions.question_stem_text: Consider two 16-point sequences x[n] and h[n]. Let the linear convolution of x[n] and h[n] be denoted by y[n], while z[n] denotes the 16-point inverse discrete Fourier transform (IDFT) of the product of the 16-point DFTs of x[n] and h[n]. The value(s) of k for which z[k] = y[k] is/are
questions.human_calibration_status: VERIFIED_ORGANIZING_INSTITUTE
questions.reviewer_audit_notes: Linear convolution y[n] has non-zero duration 0 to 30 (length 31). Circular convolution z[k] = sum_m y[k + 16m] = y[k] + y[k+16]. For k = 0..14, k+16 is in [16..30] which causes aliasing. For k = 15, k+16 = 31 where y[31] = 0 identically. Hence z[15] = y[15] without aliasing. Verified with official key C.

questions.human_calibration_status: VERIFIED_ORGANIZING_INSTITUTE

Steady state: n = n0 + Delta n approx 10^16 cm^-3, p = p0 + Delta p = 2 * 10^16 cm^-3. Product np = (10^16) * (2 * 10^16) = 2 * 10^32 cm^-6. Verified with official key D.

questions.human_calibration_status: VERIFIED_ORGANIZING_INSTITUTE
